To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ds transposition from extrachromosomally replicating vector DNA occurs during vector DNA replication in the nucleus of maize protoplasts.
Ds excision is a coupled process to vector DNA replication and that the coupling is dependent upon the presence of the transposase protein.
the frequency of Ds excisions from extrachromosomally replicating geminivirus vector DNAs was at least 3 orders of magnitude higher than that from nonreplicating DNAs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms by which the maize Activator (Ac), a member of the transposable elements, excises from its chromosomal insertion sites.
the mechanism of Ds excission from extrachromosomally replicating vector DNA.
the mechanism by which transposable elements are mobilized in maize.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ds excises from the P locus during replication of the P element.
the Ds excision frequency is increased in a DNA replication-coupled process.
Ds excision occurs during replication of the vector DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ds excision in maize is coupled to vector replication in maize.
the frequency of excision from a replicating vector is at least 10(5) times higher than from nonreplicating DNA.
Ds excision occurs during vector DNA replication in the nucleus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maize transposon system can be adapted to the study of geminivirus DNA replication and gene expression in plants.
the maize Ac/Ds transposon system can be used for gene tagging and mutagenesis of maize genes by mobilizing a geminivirus vector in maize protoplasts and in planta.
the maize Ds transposable element excises from replicating vector DNAs more than 3 x 105-fold more frequently than from nonreplicating DNAs in maize.
